input: Enroll in a court reporting or stenography taster class

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A true taster/trial class is very different from enrolling in a full introductory course module — knowing which they mean shapes what to search for and commit to.
Whether they want in-person or online learning dramatically changes which providers and geographic options are relevant.
Knowing if this is for themselves or someone else (e.g. a teenager exploring careers) affects the level, tone, and type of program needed.
Budget determines whether they look at free YouTube/community resources, paid short courses, or accredited programs with fees.
Whether they already own a stenotype machine or are starting from zero changes what equipment-inclusive programs they need to find.
Court reporting spans traditional stenography (machine), voice writing, and digital reporting — knowing their interest narrows the class type significantly.
If the goal is pure curiosity vs. testing aptitude before committing to a full program, the depth and follow-up plan for the class will differ.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a stenography taster class
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and sign up for a beginner or introductory court reporting or stenography class to explore the field.

questions.title: Is this a one-off taster session or a short course?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a single trial/taster session (e.g. 1–2 hours) or a short multi-week introductory course to get a proper feel for the skill.

questions.title: Do you want an online class or in-person training?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs a local, in-person venue or is open to fully remote/online options, which broadens provider choices significantly.

questions.title: Who is this class for — you or someone else?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is enrolling themselves or arranging this for another person, such as a student or career-changer, as this affects program suitability.

questions.title: What is your budget for this taster class?
questions.description: Understand the spending limit so the plan can focus on free resources, low-cost community college options, or paid professional short courses accordingly.

questions.title: Do you already own a stenotype machine or steno software?
questions.description: Find out if the user has any equipment, since some classes require a physical steno machine while others use free software like Plover on a regular keyboard.

questions.title: Are you drawn to machine stenography, voice writing, or digital reporting?
questions.description: Identify which branch of court reporting interests the user most, as each has distinct training paths and class types available.

questions.title: Is this to satisfy curiosity or evaluate a career change?
questions.description: Determine whether the taster is purely exploratory or part of a serious evaluation before committing to a full accredited court reporting program.
